newsitem.title: BARBADOS: CRICKET-WEST INDIES OFFER CONTRACTS TO LEADING PLAYERS.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-WEST INDIES OFFER CONTRACTS TO LEADING PLAYERS.

text.p: West Indies Cricket Board of Control (WICBC) have offered one-year contracts to 20 leading players to encourage them to stay at home to play and coach, a newspaper report said on Tuesday.
The Daily Nation added that another 30 players would be contracted over the next five years.
The initial contracts, which run from October 1 to next August 31, were reportedly worth between $15,000 and $60,000, depending on the player's test and first-class status.
"Our first contracts have gone out to potential West Indies players," WICBC chief executive officer Steve Camacho was quoted as saying.

"The other contracts will go to players of worth and quality who may not be West Indies players, but are very good first-class players and contribute enormously to the quality of the first-class game in the West Indies."
The paper said the 20 players contracted include the 16 who will tour Australia starting next month, along with opener Stuart Williams, and fast bowlers Ottis Gibson, Cameron Cuffy and Colin Stuart.
Williams, Gibson, Cuffy and Stuart are members of the West Indies A team which tours Sri Lanka later this year.
English county side Gloucestershire said on Wednesday they were confident West Indies captain Courtney Walsh would continue playing with the team.
Gloucestershire chief executive Philip August said Walsh would return to England next year to start a fresh two-year contract with the county.

"I spoke to Courtney on Monday and have also had discussions with officials at the West Indies Board," he said. "They would like to put certain players on a one-year contract but nobody will be forced to sign.
"And if some players decide to return to county cricket they will certainly not be penalised by the West Indies authorities."
All-rounder Carl Hooper is another player committed to returning to his county, Kent, next season. Hooper is currently in the middle of a two-year contract.
